pyq_focus: Is unit se NET mein sabse zyada theorist-work matching aata hai: kaun sa book kisne likha (Of Grammatology - Derrida, Orientalism - Said, Gender Trouble - Butler).
Coined terms bahut puchhe jaate hain: differance, episteme, interpellation, gynocriticism, ecriture feminine, intertextuality, hybridity, historiographic metafiction, heteroglossia, chronotope.
Famous quotes ka source pucha jaata hai: 'There is nothing outside the text', 'incredulity toward metanarratives', 'Always historicize!', 'The subaltern cannot speak'.
Chronology questions aate hain: books ko saal ke hisaab se arrange karna (Second Sex 1949 se Gender Trouble 1990 tak). Har major book ka saal yaad rakho.
Assertion-Reason mein concept ki samajh check hoti hai, jaise Saussure ka arbitrary sign, Lacan ka unconscious as language, Althusser ka ISA.
Feminism aur Postcolonialism se har saal 2-3 sawaal pakke hain; Showalter ke 3 phases, Spivak, Bhabha, Fanon, Ngugi ko achhe se padho.
Naye topics (Ecocriticism, Queer theory, Postmodernism) se 2018 ke baad sawaal badhe hain: Rueckert, Glotfelty, Buell, Sedgwick, de Lauretis, Baudrillard.
Preparation tip: har theorist ke liye ek card banao - 2 books + saal + 1 coined term + 1 quote. Is file ke works, quotes aur people lists ko roz revise karo.

easy.title: Structuralism and Narratology: Saussure, Levi-Strauss, Jakobson, Genette
easy.story: Socho cricket ke rules. Ek akela ball ka koi matlab nahi, matlab tab banta hai jab poora game ka system ho. Saussure ne kaha bhasha bhi aisi hi hai: 'kutta' shabd aur asli kutte ka rishta manmana (arbitrary) hai, aur har shabd ka matlab doosre shabdon se farak se aata hai. Langue poora system hai, parole ek baar bola gaya vaakya. Levi-Strauss ne yahi trick myths par lagayi (mythemes), Propp ne folk tales ke 31 functions gine, aur Genette ne kahani sunane ke tareeqe (focalization, order, voice) ka hisaab lagaya.
easy.trick: 'SaLe JaGe Pro' - Saussure 1916 (Course), Levi-Strauss 1958 (Structural Anthropology), Jakobson 1956/1960, Genette 1972 (Narrative Discourse), Propp 1928 (31 functions). Todorov ne 'narratology' naam rakha - 'Todo-rov ne naam todd ke rakha'.

easy.title: Roland Barthes: from structuralism to post-structuralism
easy.story: Barthes pehle structuralist the, phir khud hi structure todne lage. Mythologies mein unhone dikhaya ki ek magazine cover par salute karta Black soldier ek 'myth' banata hai - France ki empire achhi hai. Phir 1967 mein bole 'Author mar gaya' - matlab kahani ka matlab likhne wale ki marzi se nahi, padhne wale se banta hai, jaise WhatsApp forward ka matlab har koi apne hisaab se nikalta hai. S/Z mein Balzac ki Sarrasine ko 5 codes mein toda, aur readerly (aaram se padho) vs writerly (khud matlab banao) text ka farak bataya.
easy.trick: Barthes ka ladder: 'Myth-57, Death-67, S/Z-70, Pleasure-73, Camera-80'. S/Z ke 5 codes: 'HP SSC' - Hermeneutic, Proairetic, Semic, Symbolic, Cultural.

easy.title: Post-structuralism and Deconstruction: Jacques Derrida
easy.story: Dictionary mein ek shabd ka matlab dekho, wahan aur shabd milte hain, unka matlab dekho to aur shabd - matlab kabhi final nahi hota. Derrida ne isse 'differance' kaha: matlab alag bhi hota hai aur aage tal bhi jaata hai. Unhone kaha Western philosophy speech ko writing se upar rakhti hai (logocentrism) aur aise hi 'man upar, woman neeche' jaise jode banati hai. Deconstruction in jodon ko ulat-palat karke dikhata hai ki text khud apne khilaaf bolta hai. 1966 mein Johns Hopkins wala paper aur 1967 ki teen books se yeh shuru hua.
easy.trick: '66 mein khel (Play), 67 mein teen kitaabein (Grammatology, Writing and Difference, Speech and Phenomena)'. Differance mein 'a' sirf likhne mein dikhta hai, bolne mein nahi - 'a = andar chhupa'.

easy.title: Michel Foucault: discourse, power, knowledge
easy.story: School mein teacher sab bachchon ko dekh sakti hai, par bachche nahi jaante kab dekha ja raha hai, isliye sab khud hi seedhe baithte hain. Foucault ne isse Panopticon kaha - power sirf danda nahi, woh hamein andar se discipline sikhati hai. Unke liye power aur knowledge saath chalte hain: jo 'pagal', 'mareez' ya 'apradhi' kehlata hai, woh discourse banata hai. Har yug ka apna knowledge ka dhaancha hota hai jise woh episteme kehte hain.
easy.trick: Foucault ka time-table: 'Madness 61, Clinic 63, Order 66, Archaeology 69, Discipline 75, Sexuality 76' - 'Pagal-Doctor-Order-Khudai-Jail-Sex'.

easy.title: Psychoanalytic criticism: Freud, Jung, Bloom
easy.story: Freud kehte the hamare mann mein ek chhupa basement hai - unconscious - jahan dabaye hue sapne aur ichchhayein rehti hain. Sapne unhe chhupa ke dikhate hain: condensation (kai cheezein ek mein) aur displacement (dhyan doosri cheez par). Jung ne kaha poori insaaniyat ka ek common basement hai - collective unconscious - jismein archetypes hain jaise hero, maa, shadow. Harold Bloom ne kaha bada kavi apne purane guru-kavi se darr kar unhe jaan-bujh kar galat padhta hai - The Anxiety of Influence.
easy.trick: Freud = 'Dream 1900', Jung = 'Jungle of Archetypes', Bloom 1973 ke 6 ratios: 'CTK DAA' - Clinamen, Tessera, Kenosis, Daemonization, Askesis, Apophrades.

easy.title: Jacques Lacan
easy.story: Chhota bachcha pehli baar mirror mein apne aap ko dekh kar khush hota hai - 'yeh main hoon, poora aur perfect!' - par asal mein woh abhi theek se chal bhi nahi sakta. Lacan ne isse mirror stage kaha: hamara 'main' ek galatfehmi se shuru hota hai. Phir bachcha bhasha seekhta hai aur Symbolic order mein aata hai, jahan papa ka niyam (Name-of-the-Father) chalta hai. Lacan ke liye unconscious bhi ek bhasha ki tarah bana hai.
easy.trick: Teen orders ka 'ISR' = 'Imaginary, Symbolic, Real' - socho 'ISRO' ka rocket bina O ke. Mirror stage 1936/1949, Ecrits 1966.

easy.title: Marxist criticism: Althusser, Macherey, Williams and the Frankfurt School
easy.story: Marx ne kaha paisa aur kaam (base) upar ki cheezon - kala, dharm, kanoon (superstructure) - ko shape deta hai. Althusser ne bataya ki school, family, TV jaise Ideological State Apparatuses hamein chupchaap 'achha nagrik' banate hain - jaise kisi ne 'Oye!' bola aur tum mud gaye, yahi interpellation hai. Macherey ne kaha text jo nahi bolta, woh bhi important hai. Raymond Williams ne kaha 'culture is ordinary', aur Frankfurt School ne movies-music ki 'culture industry' ki aalochna ki.
easy.trick: 'Al-ISA-70' - Althusser ka ISA essay 1970. 'Gramsci = Gram-hegemony' (sahmati se raaj). 'Benjamin ki aura kho gayi photocopy mein' (1935/36).

easy.title: Marxist criticism: Terry Eagleton and Fredric Jameson
easy.story: Eagleton British hain jinhone sabke liye Literary Theory: An Introduction (1983) likhi - unke hisaab se 'literature' koi pakki cheez nahi, logon ki pasand-napasand se banta hai. Jameson American hain jinka naara hai 'Always historicize!' - har kahani ke peeche itihaas dekho. Jameson ne postmodernism ko 'late capitalism ka cultural logic' kaha, jaise mall mein sab kuch chamkila par gehraai nahi. Unhone third-world novels ko 'national allegory' bhi kaha.
easy.trick: 'E-83, J-81' - Eagleton ki Intro 1983, Jameson ki Political Unconscious 1981. Jameson = 'Jam-history' - har cheez ko itihaas ke jam mein daalo.

easy.title: Reader-response and Reception theory
easy.story: Ek hi film ko dadi, papa aur aap alag-alag tarah samajhte ho - yahi reader-response hai. Iser kehte hain text mein khaali jagah (gaps) hoti hai jo reader bharta hai. Jauss kehte hain har zamane ke padhne walon ki ek 'horizon of expectations' hoti hai. Stanley Fish kehte hain matlab akele reader se nahi, 'interpretive community' (jaise ek class ya group) se banta hai.
easy.trick: 'I-J-F' = 'Iser ke gaps, Jauss ka horizon, Fish ki community'. Rosenblatt ka 'transaction' - jaise UPI transaction, dono taraf se lena-dena.

easy.title: Feminist criticism: Beauvoir, Showalter, Gilbert and Gubar
easy.story: Beauvoir ne 1949 mein kaha ladki paida nahi hoti, samaj use 'aurat' banata hai, aur aurat ko 'Other' bana deta hai. Showalter ne women's writing ke teen phase bataye - Feminine (nakal), Feminist (virodh), Female (apni pehchaan). Gilbert aur Gubar ne kaha 19th century ki lekhikaon ne apna gussa 'pagal aurat' jaise Jane Eyre ki Bertha ke zariye dikhaya. Kate Millett ne Sexual Politics mein male writers ki aalochna ki.
easy.trick: Showalter ke phases: 'FFF = 1840-1880-1920' - 'Fashion, Fight, Freedom'. Madwoman 1979 - 'Attic mein 79 seedhiyan'.

easy.title: French feminism and Judith Butler
easy.story: French feminists ne kaha bhasha khud mardana hai, isliye aurat ko apne sharir aur apni tarah se likhna chahiye - Cixous ne isse ecriture feminine kaha ('white ink' se likhna). Kristeva ne semiotic (maa jaisi lay, rhythm) aur symbolic (papa jaisa niyam) ka farak bataya. Irigaray ne kaha aurat ki sexuality ek nahi, anek hai. Judith Butler ne kaha gender roz ki acting jaisa hai - jaise roz same uniform pehen ke role nibhana - yahi performativity hai.
easy.trick: 'Cixous ki Medusa hansti hai (1975), Kristeva ki Horror (1980), Irigaray ka Speculum (1974), Butler ka Trouble (1990)'.

easy.title: Postcolonialism: Said, Spivak, Bhabha
easy.story: Angrezon ne kitaabon mein 'East' ko jadui, aalsi aur rahasyamay dikhaya - Said ne kaha yeh Orient asli nahi, West ka banaya hua hai (Orientalism, 1978). Spivak ne poocha kya sabse neeche dabaya hua insaan, subaltern, apni baat keh sakta hai, aur sati ka udaharan diya. Bhabha ne kaha colonized log angrezon ki nakal karte hain par 'bilkul same nahi' - is mimicry aur hybridity se colonial power hil jaati hai. Teeno ko postcolonial theory ki 'Holy Trinity' kehte hain.
easy.trick: 'SSB = Said 78, Spivak 85/88, Bhabha 94' - jaise SSB interview, teeno pass karne padte hain.

easy.title: Postcolonialism: Fanon, Ngugi and others
easy.story: Fanon Martinique ke doctor the jinhone dekha ki colonized insaan 'safed mask' pehen ke jeena seekh leta hai - Black Skin, White Masks (1952). The Wretched of the Earth (1961) mein unhone azaadi ki ladaai par likha, preface Sartre ka hai. Ngugi ne kaha apni maa-bhasha mein likho, isliye English chhod ke Gikuyu mein likhne lage - Decolonising the Mind (1986). Achebe ne Conrad ke Heart of Darkness ko racist kaha.
easy.trick: 'Fanon ke 52 masks, 61 wretched' aur 'Ngugi 86 - English ko alvida'. Empire Writes Back (1989) = 'ATG' - Ashcroft, Griffiths, Tiffin.

easy.title: New Historicism and Cultural Materialism
easy.story: Shakespeare ka play padhte waqt uske zamane ke akhbaar, sarkari order, doctor ki diary bhi saath padho - yahi New Historicism hai. Greenblatt ne kaha sarkar thoda vidroh hone deti hai taaki use control kar sake (subversion-containment). Montrose ne kaha 'texts ki historicity aur history ki textuality'. British Cultural Materialism (Dollimore, Sinfield) Marxist hai aur kehta hai purane text ko aaj ki rajneeti ke liye use karo.
easy.trick: 'Greenblatt 82 mein naam, Political Shakespeare 85 mein kaam' - America = containment, Britain = dissidence.

easy.title: Ecocriticism
easy.story: Jaise hum kahani mein hero-heroine ko dekhte hain, ecocriticism nadi, jungle, mausam aur jaanwaron ko dekhta hai. Rueckert ne 1978 mein yeh shabd banaya, aur Glotfelty ne kaha yeh literature aur physical environment ke rishte ka adhyayan hai. Buell ne Thoreau par likha, Jonathan Bate ne Wordsworth ko 'green' kavi dikhaya. Amitav Ghosh ne poocha ki climate change hamare novels mein kyun nahi dikhta.
easy.trick: 'R-78, G-96' - Rueckert ne naam rakha, Glotfelty ne Reader banaya. 'Naess = Deep, d'Eaubonne = Eco-feminism'.

easy.title: Postmodernism: Lyotard, Baudrillard, Hutcheon
easy.story: Pehle log maante the ek badi kahani sab samjha degi - jaise progress ya science. Lyotard ne kaha postmodern insaan aisi grand stories par shak karta hai aur chhoti-chhoti kahaniyon par jeeta hai. Baudrillard ne kaha aaj copy asli se zyada asli lagti hai - jaise Instagram filter wali photo - yahi hyperreality hai. Hutcheon ne woh novels pehchane jo itihaas likhte hue khud par hanste hain - historiographic metafiction, jaise Midnight's Children.
easy.trick: 'L-79, B-81, H-88' - Lyotard ki Condition, Baudrillard ka Simulacra, Hutcheon ki Poetics. 'Disneyland nakli dikhaya taaki baaki America asli lage'.

easy.title: Mikhail Bakhtin and the Bakhtin Circle
easy.story: Ek shaadi mein chacha, mama, dost, pandit sab apni-apni bhasha bolte hain - novel bhi aisa hi hai, Bakhtin ne isse heteroglossia kaha. Dostoevsky ke novels mein har character ki awaaz azaad hai, author sab par haavi nahi - yeh polyphony hai. Holi jaisa tyohaar jismein raja-praja ka farak mit jaata hai - Bakhtin isse carnivalesque kehte hain (Rabelais par). Time aur space ka jod chronotope hai, jaise 'road' kahani mein milne ka time-space.
easy.trick: 'Dosto 29/63 = Polyphony, Rabelais 65 = Carnival, Dialogic 75/81 = Heteroglossia + Chronotope'. Bakhtin = 'Baat-chit' (dialogism).

easy.title: Queer theory
easy.story: Samaj maan ke chalta hai ki har koi straight hai aur ladka-ladki ka role fix hai - isse heteronormativity kehte hain. Queer theory kehti hai sexuality aur gender fixed label nahi, samaj ke banaye hue hain. Foucault ne kaha 'homosexual' ek identity ke roop mein 19th century mein bana. Sedgwick ne male dosti ke andar ke rishton (homosocial desire) aur 'closet' ki baat ki, aur Teresa de Lauretis ne 1990 mein 'queer theory' naam diya.
easy.trick: 'Sedgwick 85 Between Men, 90 Closet; de Lauretis 90/91 naam; Butler 90 Trouble' - 1990 queer theory ka janam saal.

quotes.quote: In language there are only differences without positive terms.
The linguistic sign unites, not a thing and a name, but a concept and a sound-image.
The bond between the signifier and the signified is arbitrary.
The poetic function projects the principle of equivalence from the axis of selection into the axis of combination.
The birth of the reader must be at the cost of the death of the Author.
The text is a tissue of quotations drawn from the innumerable centres of culture.
There is nothing outside the text (il n'y a pas de hors-texte).
The absence of the transcendental signified extends the domain and the play of signification infinitely.
quotes.source: Structure, Sign and Play in the Discourse of the Human Sciences (1966)

quotes.quote: Man is an invention of recent date. And one perhaps nearing its end.
What difference does it make who is speaking?
Visibility is a trap.
Where there is power, there is resistance.
The sodomite had been a temporary aberration; the homosexual was now a species.
Where id was, there ego shall be.
Poetic history is held to be indistinguishable from poetic influence, since strong poets make that history by misreading one another, so as to clear imaginative space for themselves.
The unconscious is structured like a language.
Man's desire is the desire of the Other.
Ideology represents the imaginary relationship of individuals to their real conditions of existence.
Ideology has no history.
Culture is ordinary.
There is no document of civilization which is not at the same time a document of barbarism.
quotes.source: Theses on the Philosophy of History (1940)

quotes.quote: Always historicize!
Pastiche is thus blank parody, a statue with blind eyeballs.
quotes.source: Postmodernism, or, The Cultural Logic of Late Capitalism (1984/1991)

quotes.quote: Literature is a kind of writing which, in the words of Roman Jakobson, represents an 'organized violence committed on ordinary speech'.
Interpretive communities are made up of those who share interpretive strategies not for reading but for writing texts.
quotes.source: Is There a Text in This Class? (1980)

quotes.quote: One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.
A woman must have money and a room of her own if she is to write fiction.
Is a pen a metaphorical penis?
Woman must write her self.
Any text is constructed as a mosaic of quotations; any text is the absorption and transformation of another.
Gender is the repeated stylization of the body, a set of repeated acts within a highly rigid regulatory frame that congeal over time to produce the appearance of substance.
There is no gender identity behind the expressions of gender; that identity is performatively constituted by the very 'expressions' that are said to be its results.
The Orient was almost a European invention.
The subaltern cannot speak.
White men are saving brown women from brown men.
Colonial mimicry is the desire for a reformed, recognizable Other, as a subject of a difference that is almost the same, but not quite.
quotes.source: Of Mimicry and Man (1984), in The Location of Culture (1994)

quotes.quote: For the black man there is only one destiny. And it is white.
Each generation must, out of relative obscurity, discover its mission, fulfil it, or betray it.
Language carries culture, and culture carries, particularly through orature and literature, the entire body of values by which we come to perceive ourselves and our place in the world.
Conrad was a thoroughgoing racist.
quotes.source: An Image of Africa (1975 lecture, revised 1977)

quotes.quote: I began with the desire to speak with the dead.
The historicity of texts and the textuality of history.
Ecocriticism is the study of the relationship between literature and the physical environment.
Simplifying to the extreme, I define postmodern as incredulity toward metanarratives.
The territory no longer precedes the map, nor does it survive it. It is nevertheless the map that precedes the territory.
Disneyland is presented as imaginary in order to make us believe that the rest is real.
The word in language is half someone else's.
quotes.source: Discourse in the Novel (1934-35), in The Dialogic Imagination

quotes.quote: People are different from each other.

people.note: Founder of psychoanalysis; unconscious, Oedipus complex

people.note: Freud's biographer; Oedipal reading of Hamlet

people.note: Canadian critic; archetypal or myth criticism

people.name: Norman Holland
people.note: American psychoanalytic reader-response critic; identity theme

people.name: Jacques Lacan
people.note: French psychoanalyst; mirror stage, Imaginary-Symbolic-Real

people.name: Laura Mulvey
people.note: British film theorist; coined the male gaze

people.name: Slavoj Zizek
people.note: Slovenian thinker; popularises Lacan through popular culture

people.name: Louis Althusser
people.note: French Marxist; interpellation, ISA/RSA

people.name: Pierre Macherey

people.name: Georg Lukacs

people.name: Antonio Gramsci

people.name: Raymond Williams

people.name: Theodor Adorno

people.name: Stuart Hall

people.name: Terry Eagleton

people.name: Fredric Jameson
people.note: American Marxist; Always historicize, late capitalism

people.name: Louise Rosenblatt
people.where: The Reader, the Text, the Poem (1978)
people.note: American; transactional theory, efferent vs aesthetic reading

people.name: Wolfgang Iser
people.note: Konstanz School; implied reader, gaps

people.name: Hans Robert Jauss

people.name: Stanley Fish

people.name: Umberto Eco

people.name: Wayne Booth
people.note: Chicago critic; implied author, unreliable narrator

people.name: Simone de Beauvoir

people.name: Kate Millett
people.note: American feminist; patriarchy in male writers

people.name: Elaine Showalter
people.note: American; gynocriticism, three phases

people.name: Sandra Gilbert and Susan Gubar

people.name: Alice Walker

people.name: Helene Cixous

people.name: Luce Irigaray

people.name: Judith Butler

people.name: Edward Said

people.name: Homi K. Bhabha
people.note: Indian-born theorist; hybridity, mimicry, Third Space

people.name: Frantz Fanon
people.note: Martinican psychiatrist; colonial psychology, decolonization

people.name: Ngugi wa Thiong'o

people.name: Chinua Achebe

people.name: Aime Cesaire

people.note: American; coined New Historicism, cultural poetics

people.name: Louis Montrose

people.name: Clifford Geertz

people.name: Lawrence Buell
people.note: American; waves of ecocriticism

people.name: Jean-Francois Lyotard
people.note: French; incredulity toward metanarratives

people.name: Jean Baudrillard
people.note: French; simulacra and hyperreality

people.name: Linda Hutcheon
people.note: Canadian; historiographic metafiction

mcqs.q: Writing Degree Zero (1953) was written by:
mcqs.exp: Barthes ki pehli kitaab, 1953 - writing ki 'zero degree' style.

mcqs.q: 'The World of Wrestling' is the opening essay of:
mcqs.exp: Barthes ki Mythologies (1957) mein wrestling, wine, toys par essays hain.

mcqs.q: Gerard Genette's Narrative Discourse is built mainly on a reading of:
options: Proust's In Search of Lost Time
mcqs.exp: Genette ne order, duration, frequency, mood, voice Proust par samjhaaye.

mcqs.q: In Genette's terms, a narrator who is also a character in the story he tells is:
mcqs.exp: Homo = same: narrator kahani ke andar maujood hai.

mcqs.q: How many functions does Vladimir Propp identify in Morphology of the Folktale?
mcqs.exp: Propp: 31 functions aur 7 spheres of action.

mcqs.q: In Of Grammatology Derrida develops the logic of the 'supplement' through a reading of:
mcqs.exp: Rousseau writing ko speech ka 'dangerous supplement' kehte hain.

mcqs.q: Derrida's essay 'Plato's Pharmacy' appears in:
mcqs.exp: Dissemination (1972) mein pharmakon = dawa bhi, zeher bhi.

mcqs.q: Allegories of Reading (1979) was written by:
mcqs.exp: Paul de Man, Yale School ka deconstructionist.

mcqs.q: The concept of the 'author function' is proposed in Foucault's:
mcqs.exp: 'What Is an Author?' (1969) - author ek discourse ka function hai.

mcqs.q: In The History of Sexuality, Volume 1, Foucault questions:
mcqs.exp: Foucault: Victorian daur mein sex dabaaya nahi, uske baare mein discourse badha.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT one of Harold Bloom's revisionary ratios?
mcqs.exp: Bloom ke 6 ratios: clinamen, tessera, kenosis, daemonization, askesis, apophrades. Catharsis Aristotle ka hai.

mcqs.q: For Carl Jung, archetypes reside in the:
mcqs.exp: Jung: archetypes poori insaaniyat ke saanjhe collective unconscious mein.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT one of Lacan's three orders?
mcqs.exp: Semiotic Kristeva ka term hai; Lacan: Imaginary, Symbolic, Real.

mcqs.q: Lacan's seminar, critiqued by Derrida in 'The Purveyor of Truth', reads:
options: James's The Turn of the Screw
Poe's The Fall of the House of Usher
mcqs.exp: Lacan ka Seminar on 'The Purloined Letter'; Derrida ne jawab diya.

mcqs.q: Freud's essay 'The Uncanny' (1919) discusses:
mcqs.exp: Uncanny = jaana-pehchaana jo ajeeb lage; Sandman ki kahani.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a Repressive State Apparatus for Althusser?
mcqs.exp: RSA force se chalta hai (police, army); church, school, family ISA hain.

mcqs.q: The concept of 'structure of feeling' is associated with:
mcqs.exp: Williams: ek daur ka jiya hua anubhav, structure of feeling.

mcqs.q: The term 'culture industry' was introduced by:
mcqs.exp: Dialectic of Enlightenment mein 'The Culture Industry' chapter.

mcqs.q: The decline of the 'aura' of the artwork is discussed by:
mcqs.exp: Benjamin, 'The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction' (1936).

mcqs.q: Hegemony as rule by consent rather than force is a key concept of:
mcqs.exp: Gramsci ki Prison Notebooks.

mcqs.q: Fredric Jameson describes postmodern pastiche as:
options: A simulacrum of the third order
mcqs.exp: Jameson: pastiche = bina vyangya ki nakal, 'blank parody'.

mcqs.q: Criticism and Ideology (1976) was written by:
mcqs.exp: Eagleton ki 1976 ki Marxist kitaab.

mcqs.q: The idea that the reader fills 'gaps' or 'blanks' in the text is central to:
mcqs.exp: Iser: The Implied Reader, The Act of Reading.

mcqs.q: The concept of 'interpretive communities' belongs to:
mcqs.exp: Fish: meaning reader ki community tay karti hai.

mcqs.q: Iser and Jauss are associated with the:
mcqs.exp: Dono Konstanz University (Germany) se - reception theory.

mcqs.q: Norman Holland's psychoanalytic reader-response theory centres on the reader's:
mcqs.exp: Holland, 5 Readers Reading (1975).

mcqs.q: In The Second Sex, Beauvoir argues that man is the Subject and woman is:
mcqs.exp: 'He is the Subject, he is the Absolute - she is the Other.'

mcqs.q: Showalter coined 'gynocriticism' in the essay:
mcqs.exp: Towards a Feminist Poetics (1979): gynocritics = women as writers.

mcqs.q: Which writer is NOT among those attacked in Kate Millett's Sexual Politics?
mcqs.exp: Millett ne Lawrence, Miller, Mailer aur Genet ki aalochana ki.

mcqs.q: The title The Madwoman in the Attic refers to a character from:
mcqs.exp: Bertha Mason, Rochester ki pagal patni, attic mein band.

mcqs.q: Kristeva's distinction between the semiotic and the symbolic is developed in:
mcqs.exp: Revolution in Poetic Language (1974).

mcqs.q: Bodies That Matter (1993) was written by:
mcqs.exp: Butler ki Gender Trouble ke baad ki kitaab.

mcqs.q: Said's notion of Orientalism as a discourse draws chiefly on:
mcqs.exp: Said ne Foucault ka discourse aur Gramsci ka hegemony use kiya.

mcqs.q: In Culture and Imperialism, Said reads the Antigua plantation in:
mcqs.exp: Sir Thomas Bertram ki Antigua estate - contrapuntal reading.

mcqs.q: Who translated Derrida's Of Grammatology into English (1976)?
mcqs.exp: Spivak ka lamba translator's preface mashhoor hai.

mcqs.q: The concept of the 'Third Space' of enunciation belongs to:
mcqs.exp: Bhabha, The Location of Culture (1994): hybridity, Third Space.

mcqs.q: The preface to Fanon's The Wretched of the Earth was written by:
mcqs.exp: Sartre ne 1961 mein preface likha.

mcqs.q: In Decolonising the Mind, Ngugi announces he will write in:
mcqs.exp: Ngugi ne English chhodkar Gikuyu apnaayi.

mcqs.q: Negritude is chiefly associated with:
mcqs.exp: Cesaire aur Senghor - Black identity ka French-language movement.

mcqs.q: The term 'strategic essentialism' is associated with:
mcqs.exp: Spivak: political maqsad ke liye kuch der identity ko ek maan lena.

mcqs.q: Match the theorists with their terms: (a) Derrida (b) Foucault (c) Althusser (d) Bhabha -- (i) interpellation (ii) differance (iii) hybridity (iv) episteme
mcqs.exp: Derrida-differance, Foucault-episteme, Althusser-interpellation, Bhabha-hybridity.

mcqs.q: Match the works with their authors: (a) Simulacra and Simulation (b) The Postmodern Condition (c) A Poetics of Postmodernism (d) Postmodernism, or, The Cultural Logic of Late Capitalism -- (i) Lyotard (ii) Jameson (iii) Baudrillard (iv) Hutcheon
mcqs.exp: Baudrillard 1981, Lyotard 1979, Hutcheon 1988, Jameson 1991.

mcqs.q: Match the ecocritics with their works: (a) Cheryll Glotfelty (b) William Rueckert (c) Lawrence Buell (d) Greg Garrard -- (i) The Environmental Imagination (ii) Literature and Ecology: An Experiment in Ecocriticism (iii) Ecocriticism (New Critical Idiom) (iv) The Ecocriticism Reader (co-edited)
mcqs.exp: Glotfelty-Reader 1996, Rueckert-1978 essay, Buell-1995, Garrard-2004.

mcqs.q: Match the Bakhtin-circle texts with what they are known for: (a) Problems of Dostoevsky's Poetics (b) Rabelais and His World (c) The Dialogic Imagination (d) Marxism and the Philosophy of Language -- (i) heteroglossia (ii) published under V. N. Voloshinov's name (iii) polyphony (iv) carnival
mcqs.exp: Dostoevsky-polyphony, Rabelais-carnival, Dialogic-heteroglossia, Voloshinov ke naam se Marxism and the Philosophy of Language.

mcqs.q: Match the critics with their works or phrases: (a) Stephen Greenblatt (b) Louis Montrose (c) Jonathan Dollimore (d) Alan Sinfield -- (i) Radical Tragedy (ii) Renaissance Self-Fashioning (iii) Faultlines (iv) 'the textuality of history and the historicity of texts'
mcqs.exp: Greenblatt 1980, Montrose ka mashhoor phrase, Dollimore 1984, Sinfield 1992.

mcqs.q: Match the thinkers with their works: (a) Freud (b) Jung (c) Lacan (d) Bloom -- (i) Ecrits (ii) The Interpretation of Dreams (iii) The Anxiety of Influence (iv) The Archetypes and the Collective Unconscious
mcqs.exp: Freud 1900, Jung archetypes, Lacan 1966, Bloom 1973.

mcqs.q: Match the feminist critics with their works: (a) Toril Moi (b) Elaine Showalter (c) Kate Millett (d) Adrienne Rich -- (i) Sexual Politics (ii) Compulsory Heterosexuality and Lesbian Existence (iii) Sexual/Textual Politics (iv) A Literature of Their Own
mcqs.exp: Moi 1985, Showalter 1977, Millett 1970, Rich 1980.

mcqs.q: Match the narratologists with their concepts: (a) Genette (b) Greimas (c) Propp (d) Todorov -- (i) actantial model (ii) focalization (iii) coined 'narratology' (iv) functions of the folktale
mcqs.exp: Genette-focalization, Greimas-actants, Propp-31 functions, Todorov-narratologie (1969).

mcqs.q: Match the queer theorists with their concepts: (a) Eve Kosofsky Sedgwick (b) Teresa de Lauretis (c) Michael Warner (d) Lee Edelman -- (i) heteronormativity (ii) homosocial desire (iii) reproductive futurism (iv) coined the term 'queer theory'
mcqs.exp: Sedgwick-Between Men, de Lauretis-1990/91, Warner-heteronormativity, Edelman-No Future.

mcqs.q: Match the Marxist critics with their works: (a) Georg Lukacs (b) Lucien Goldmann (c) Pierre Macherey (d) Walter Benjamin -- (i) The Hidden God (ii) The Historical Novel (iii) A Theory of Literary Production (iv) Illuminations
mcqs.exp: Lukacs-Historical Novel, Goldmann-Hidden God, Macherey-Literary Production, Benjamin-Illuminations.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): Saussure holds that the linguistic sign is arbitrary. Reason (R): There is no natural or necessary link between the signifier and the signified.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
mcqs.exp: R hi batata hai sign arbitrary kyon hai.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): Derrida's 'differance' combines the senses of 'to differ' and 'to defer'. Reason (R): Derrida holds that meaning is fully present in speech.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
mcqs.exp: A sahi; R galat - Derrida logocentrism aur presence ko hi challenge karte hain.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): Frantz Fanon wrote Black Skin, White Masks. Reason (R): Fanon was born in Martinique.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
mcqs.exp: Dono sach, par janm-sthaan kitaab likhne ki wajah nahi.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): Showalter's gynocriticism studies women as writers. Reason (R): Showalter's A Literature of Their Own was published in 1990.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
mcqs.exp: A sahi; A Literature of Their Own 1977 mein aayi.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): In Discipline and Punish, Foucault argues that power is held only by the sovereign. Reason (R): Foucault sees power as diffuse and productive, circulating through institutions.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
mcqs.exp: Foucault ke liye power har jagah failaa hua hai, sirf raja ke paas nahi.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): For Bhabha, colonial mimicry is ambivalent and can menace colonial authority. Reason (R): Mimicry produces a subject who is 'almost the same, but not quite'.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
mcqs.exp: 'Not quite' wala farak hi mimicry ko khatarnaak banata hai.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): Cheryll Glotfelty coined the term 'ecocriticism' in 1996. Reason (R): Glotfelty co-edited The Ecocriticism Reader.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
mcqs.exp: Term William Rueckert ne 1978 mein diya; R sahi hai.

mcqs.q: Assertion (A): Ngugi wa Thiong'o wrote Decolonising the Mind. Reason (R): Ngugi was born in Kenya.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
mcqs.exp: Dono sach, par R A ko explain nahi karta.

mcqs.q: Arrange in chronological order: (i) S/Z (ii) Course in General Linguistics (iii) Structural Anthropology (iv) Morphology of the Folktale
Arrange Foucault's works in chronological order: (i) Discipline and Punish (ii) The Order of Things (iii) The History of Sexuality, Vol. 1 (iv) Madness and Civilization
Arrange in chronological order: (i) The Madwoman in the Attic (ii) A Room of One's Own (iii) Gender Trouble (iv) Sexual Politics
Arrange in chronological order: (i) The Location of Culture (ii) Black Skin, White Masks (iii) Can the Subaltern Speak? (iv) Orientalism
Arrange in chronological order: (i) A Poetics of Postmodernism (ii) Postmodernism, or, The Cultural Logic of Late Capitalism (iii) Simulacra and Simulation (iv) The Postmodern Condition
Arrange in chronological order: (i) Ecrits (ii) Beyond the Pleasure Principle (iii) The Anxiety of Influence (iv) The Interpretation of Dreams
Arrange in chronological order: (i) The Ecocriticism Reader (ii) Silent Spring (iii) The Environmental Imagination (iv) Rueckert's 'Literature and Ecology: An Experiment in Ecocriticism'
Identify the correct statement:
options: Saussure's Course in General Linguistics was published in his lifetime.
Jakobson links metaphor with the axis of selection and metonymy with the axis of combination.
mcqs.exp: Course 1916 mein maut ke baad chhapi; narratology Todorov ka; Propp ne Russian folktales padhi.

mcqs.q: Identify the correct statement:
options: Political Shakespeare was edited by Greenblatt and Montrose.
Raymond Williams used the term 'cultural materialism'.
mcqs.exp: Political Shakespeare - Dollimore aur Sinfield; Greenblatt ne 'New Historicism' kaha.

mcqs.q: Identify the correct statement:
options: Spivak's 'Can the Subaltern Speak?' discusses the abolition of sati.
Bhabha wrote The Wretched of the Earth.
Ngugi's Decolonising the Mind argues for writing African literature in English.
mcqs.exp: Orientalism 1978; Wretched - Fanon; Ngugi ne English chhodi.

mcqs.q: Identify the correct statement:
options: Irigaray wrote 'The Laugh of the Medusa'.
Cixous, Irigaray and Kristeva are commonly grouped as French feminists.
Kristeva wrote This Sex Which Is Not One.
mcqs.exp: Medusa - Cixous; This Sex - Irigaray; Gender Trouble 1990.

mcqs.q: Identify the correct statement:
options: Rabelais and His World is a study of the Romantic lyric.
Bakhtin took Tolstoy's novels as the model of polyphony.
Bakhtin's 'chronotope' means the fusion of time and space in narrative.
mcqs.exp: Intertextuality - Kristeva; polyphony - Dostoevsky; Rabelais - carnival.
